sections.risk_rationale: Guideline prescribes specific industry use cases (object detection, financial reports with charts, medical documents) and a normative claim that native multimodal is 'a must' for enterprise AI, but depth_checklist shows gaps in case_studies_metrics, latest_advancements, and industry_applications.

Section mandates strong claims on OCR cascade errors, fragility, and failure on sketches/X-rays plus explicit note to 'Add some report numbers on this' (absent per sources), arguing it 'doesn't scale for AI agents' with thin digest coverage on limitations_failure_modes beyond generic OCR blogs.

Guideline dictates specific 2025 model families (Llama 4, GPT-5 etc.), diffusion vs LLM comparison, and trade-offs between Unified Embedding and Cross-modality Attention drawn from one primary Raschka source, exceeding the 'surface-level' and 'must stay brief' constraints.

Extremely prescriptive <define_how_the_code_should_be_explained_step_by_step> dictates verbatim sequence (load_image_as_bytes, specific WEBP/PDF 'attention_is_all_you_need_paper.pdf', Pydantic bounding boxes, kitten/robot object detection, pseudocode for GCS) that constitutes a fully authored worked example.

Guideline asserts ColPali as 'the most popular architecture' for 2025 with specific benchmark (81.3% nDCG@5), paradigm-shift claims, and late-interaction details that rest on two sources while requiring brevity on core innovation only.

Detailed numbered walkthrough mandates specific functions (create_vector_index, generate_image_description workaround, embed_text_with_gemini, search_multimodal), exact queries ('what is the architecture of the transformer neural network?', 'a kitten with a robot'), and explanation of why description is used despite lesson thesis.

Guideline scripts exact integration (multimodal_search_tool, build_react_agent with system_prompt, test_question 'what color is my kitten?', ReAct steps) as a pre-scripted capstone consolidating Part 1, using LangGraph drop-in with future-lesson caveats.
Purely transitional wrap-up referencing capstone project and Part 2 concepts (MCP, LangGraph, evaluation) at high level per anchoring rules, with no original normative leaps or thin citations.

parsed.overall_notes: Implementation sections (S4,S6,S7) are almost entirely pre-scripted code narratives using the exact notebook sequence and examples (e.g. Attention paper PDF, kitten queries), rendering further exploration irrelevant. Early sections advance a strong normative thesis against OCR in favor of native multimodal processing, but coverage gaps on metrics/case studies plus reliance on a few canonical sources (Raschka, ColPali arXiv, CLIP explanations) with high tavily saturation indicate limited new material would be found.
